definition: Goad means to prod or taunt someone into doing something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word goad. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know goad should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The parrot goaded the old cat mercilessly — a whistle, a pause, a tap on the cage bars — until the cat finally sprang and knocked over the lamp.
Teasing is far milder than goading — playful poking that wants a laugh, not a reaction.
Needling is a step short of goading — the jabs sting and repeat, but goading aims every jab at one target: making the person finally act.

To prod is to nudge someone repeatedly toward action — a poke, a reminder, another poke — without the sting. Goading keeps the pushing but adds the barb: its jabs are designed to irritate a person into moving. A prod hurries you along; a goad provokes you into reacting.

To taunt is to jeer — mockery that may not aim at any action at all; the insult itself is the point. Goading borrows the taunt's sting and gives it a destination: every jab is meant to push the target into doing something. A taunt wounds; a goad steers.
to settle someone down instead of working them up
to take the wind out of someone entirely

Goad came into English whole, as the name of the drover's pointed stick, and no other common English word shares it. The noun and the verb are the same word wearing two hats — the tool, and the taunting that works like it.
Goad means to prod or taunt someone into doing something.
The talk-show host spent the whole segment goading his guest — misquoting her book, praising her rival — until she snapped and said exactly the unguarded thing his producers wanted.
Unlike urging or encouraging, goading works through irritation: jabs, taunts, and needling designed to sting a person into moving.
The goader doesn't ask you to act — he makes staying still feel unbearable.
Goad is the word for provocation with a purpose — the needling that wants a reaction.
Use 'tease' when it's all in fun and 'taunt' when the mockery is the whole point; goad means the jabs are steering you somewhere.
Its unit-mates reach the same destination by kinder roads: exhort cheers you into acting, and galvanize shocks you into it.
